recipes.name: Bacon Appetizer Crescents
ingredients_raw: 1 (8 ounce) package PHILADELPHIA Cream Cheese, softened
8 slices OSCAR MAYER Bacon, cooked, crumbled
2 (8 ounce) packages refrigerated crescent dinner rolls

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Mix cream cheese, bacon, Parmesan cheese, onion, parsley, and milk together in a bowl.

Separate each can of dough into 8 triangles; cut each triangle lengthwise in half. Spread each dough triangle with 1 generous teaspoon cream cheese mixture; roll up, starting at short side of triangle. Place, point-side down, on baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven for 12 to 15 minutes or until golden brown. Serve warm.

raw_recipe.headline: Bacon Appetizer Crescents
raw_recipe.description: These golden crescent rolls have a bacon, cream cheese, Parmesan, and parsley filling. A delicious savory treat or party appetizer.

review.reviewBody: I've made these just spreading Herb and Garlic Philadelphia cream cheese and cooked, chopped bacon inside. Everyone always asks for more. I'vd never heard about making it with onions ect...I'll have to give that a try!

These are delicious, and they were a huge hit. Next time I make them, though, I'm going to add green chiles, just for variation. 

Variations I made this time:
1. Onion powder for the minced onions, because we're not huge fans of the onion texture in this house. The flavor was still good. 
2. Shredded Parmesan, rather than the powdered Kraft stuff.
3. Sprinkled the top with sesame seeds before baking.

These were amazing! Many requests for the recipe followed everyone devouring them. I did follow the advice of another reviewer as I was under a time crunch. I used the Pillsbury dough sheet and rolled up in a log to slice as pinwheels (same cooking time & temp apply). I used Philly chive & onion flavored cream cheese, added parm cheese, milk, bacon and some garlic powder. Thank you so much for this fabulous recipe!

These were good but I altered a few things. 1st - I used the pilsbury dough sheet and log rolled it, instead of crescent rolls. I sliced it before baking for 10 min at 375. Much easier and more consistent size for presentation this way. I added more bacon and shaved parm instead of grated. The entire group loved them! Will make again, for sure.

I have never seen anything fly off the plate as fast as these did. I was in a hurry so didn't cut the crescent rolls in half and so doubled the filling amount but it didn't matter. Cooking time was the same and they were delicious. I chose to sauté the onion (I had green onion on hand and 1/2 cup uncooked made about 1/4 cup cooked) since kids were present, as other reviewers suggested. Amazing! I will definitely make again.

I made this to take to friend's house for a Fourth of July Celebration. However, I was running late, and didn't have have to bake the crescent rolls, so I simply used ritz crackers. It turned out just fine.

Delicious! I made this exactly like the recipe except I used bacon bits (much quicker) and added a couple of large mushrooms diced really small. Everyone loved them; I will definitely make this recipe again.

This was an absolute hit at a friends party. Though I made some distinct changes. I used a thick cut of Bacon, real shredded parmisan cheese, I also cooked the onions with garlic and a touch of olive oil till the onions were translucent. It added a sweetness while accentuating the natural smokiness of the Bacon. Over all an awsome base recipe, especially with how is it is to customize.

Thank you.

Yeah, couldn't stop eating these!! I did saute onions in the bacon grease after frying the bacon. And I found flavored cream cheese instead of adding parsley to regular cream cheese. So amazingly good!
Absolutely loved these! I sauteed the onions in the bacon greese to give them a little more flavor and take out some of the bite. Will for sure be making these again.
I made this recipe with minor changes. I replaced the yellow onion with green onion, the parsley with spinach and doubled the bacon. No Parmesan or milk. Was a huge hit!
this is sooooooooo good!!
I made these the only change I put in extra bacon and an olive mix. Added green onion versus regular onion. They were a hit
Really quick and easy. Subbed scallions (green onions) for regular onions and it gave it a nice spring/summer flavor. Highly recommended!

I have made these for several different occasions and everyone always LOVES them! The only change I made was I sauteed green onions in the bacon grease to give them a little extra flavor. It really makes a difference.

I have made these for several different occasions and everyone always LOVES them! The only change I made was I sauteed green onions in the bacon grease to give them a little extra flavor. It really makes a difference.
Delicious! I sautéd the onions in bacon grease and added some ranch dressing! A party hit!

These are great and everyone always eats them up quickly. The only variation I do is cook the onions in the bacon grease after cooking the bacon. It makes a little difference but it tastes even better!
SUPER AWESOME! Would recommend that you make double the filling - so it completely fills the "mini" Crescent rolls. Any left over after that can be baked and used as chip dip!
So, delicious! My friend and I loved them! Thank you for the recipe!!!!
